sourceIssues.printed: Consider the normal surface X = Spec k[x, y, x]/(x² + xyz).
sourceIssues.correction: X = Spec k[x, y, z]/(x² + xyz), which is not normal: x² + xyz = x(x + yz), so X is the union of two smooth surfaces meeting along x = yz = 0, and its local ring at the origin is not a domain.
sourceIssues.reason: Normality is never used. The rest of the remark holds for this X: T_0X is 3-dimensional, a formal curve (f, g, h) with f(f + gh) = 0 has f = 0 or f = −gh, so f has no t-term, and the tangent cone is Spec k[x, y, z]/(x²). This matches the checkpoint's reading of [P95, Ex. 4.5], a special fibre with two smooth components meeting non-transversally.

sourceIssues.locator: published version, Forum Math. Pi 14 (2026) e14 (Cambridge repository copy, SHA-256 b3e4bf8b…); §4.2.9 and proof of Proposition 4.2.10(2), p.35
sourceIssues.printed: (ϖ, ϖ′) ∈ W(α) if X_α v_{ϖ′} ≠ 0 for some weight vector … Equivalently, (ϖ, ϖ′) ∈ W(α) if and only if ϖ′ and ϖ′ + α are weights of V(ϖ); … If we let ν and v ∈ V(ν) range over all such pairs with X_α v ≠ 0, then (ϖ, ϖ′ − α) range over all elements of W(α).
sourceIssues.correction: The equivalence fails in characteristic p, and the printed proof bounds l only over the pairs realised by a nonzero X_α. Every pair with ϖ minuscule is realised, so the argument gives l ≤ j_α (the minimum over ϖ ∈ S of Proposition 4.2.13) for (α, ⟨λ, α⟩ − l) ∈ Φ^FM. With k_α ≥ j_α from the proof of Proposition 4.2.13, this still gives Φ^cur = Φ^tan = Φ^FM, so Theorem 4.2.3 stands.
sourceIssues.reason: Here k is algebraically closed of characteristic p (§4.1.1). Take G = GL_2, α = e_1 − e_2 and ϖ = (p, 0). The Weyl module V(ϖ) has basis v_0, …, v_p with v_i of weight (p − i, i) and X_α v_i = (p − i + 1) v_{i−1}, so X_α v_1 = p·v_0 = 0 although (p − 1, 1) and (p, 0) are weights. The two readings of W(α) differ, and neither makes the last sentence of the proof true: V(ν)* is the induced module H⁰(ϖ), not V(ϖ). For ν minuscule, adjacent weights span the standard representation of the root SL_2, on which X_α is nonzero in every characteristic, so the pairs with ϖ ∈ S are realised. Proposition 4.2.10(2) for general λ ≼ μ, and the equalities with l_α in (4.2.12), Proposition 4.2.13, Remark 4.2.16 and Corollary 4.2.19, rest on the printed step and are not established by it in characteristic p. The results used later need only k_α = j_α.
